facts.value: Various activities have been initiated by different students in the past. The first point of contact to meet other students in Scandinavian studies is the Scandinavian Studies Institute Group, which meets regularly in the student council room (Q1, ground floor, R. 157).
Outside of these meetings, the student council room is open to all students in the presence of a member of the Institute Group.

The student representatives are members of the Institute Group and coordinate all activities of the group, representing the interests of the student body in the directorate and acting as contacts for issues regarding the group or communication with lecturers and staff.
The information discussion serves as a forum for students and teachers of the institute, which typically takes place once per semester.
General questions about the study program as well as specific topics can be discussed, with topics determined in close consultation with the institute management.
The Scandinavian Studies Institute Group coordinates regular student activities and events at the institute, and welcomes anyone who wants to get involved.
Meetings take place multiple times during the lecture period, and when they occur will be announced in advance via the mailing list.
The student council room (IG 157) has no special opening hours; any member of the Institute Group can obtain the key at the reception.
The Scandinavian Studies Institute Group welcomes all new students! At the beginning of each winter semester, an orientation event takes place for new students.
Subsequently, all interested are invited to go have lunch together in the cafeteria.
Beforehand, a short campus tour is offered for everyone.
Regular pub nights and game nights or days (which then have the posh name Ragnazøck) are organized.
Towards the end of each summer semester, the Midsummer Festival takes place, sometimes even outdoors in nice weather.
The Christmas Festival (Glöggfest) is a cozy event with homemade Glögg and punch in front of the institute's rooms, with the date announced in advance in the winter semester.
